Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 OBJECTIVE 2 GAMEPLAY (per round) 3 CARD VALUES 4 SPECIAL RULE: PAIRS (Sharing) 5 SCORING OBJECTIVE Achieve the lowest total score over 9 rounds (holes). Just like in real golf, a lower score is better! GAMEPLAY (per round) Each player starts with 8 cards dealt face-down in two rows in front of them. Start: Each player flips over any two of their cards. The Turn: On your turn, draw the top card from either the draw pile or the discard pile . Swap or Discard: You may swap any of your 8 cards (whether face-up or face-down) with the card you drew. The old card is placed face-up on the discard pile. If you drew from the draw pile, you may also discard the card directly face-up onto the discard pile. If you do this, you must flip over one of your face-down cards. End of Round: Once a player has flipped all 8 of their cards face-up, all other players have exactly one more turn. Then, all remaining cards are revealed. CARD VALUES -5 (Hole-in-One): The best card. 0 (Eagle): Very good. 1 to 12: These score their printed value. Stroke: Cards with "+" values (e.g., +2 or +3). SPECIAL RULE: PAIRS (Sharing) If you have two identical cards (same number) in a vertical column , that column scores 0 points (even if they are high numbers like two 12s!). Exception: Two "-5" cards in a column count as -10 points total. Double pairs A double pairs (two pairs) beside each other will score -10 SCORING After each round, the points of the 8 cards (considering pairs) are added up and recorded. The player with the lowest total sum after 9 rounds wins the game. [Rating: 1/10] This game is almost completely luck-based. As with many card games, there is often a clearly optimal choice during each turn, making you feel like you're just going through the motions for nine rounds. As far as classic card games go (variants of this can be played with a 52-card deck), Play Nine is more appealing than most. Unfortunately, that's saying almost nothing, and this game is still a hot pile of trash.

[Rating: 2/10] If you love the old card game "Golf" this is going to blow your mind!  For the rest of us this is pretty much worthless.  Draw a card, see what you get replace unknown quantities for known quantities.  Hope that you draw well, or that the player before you discards to your advantage.  I don't hate it the way I do Rat-A-Tat-Cat, but perhaps RATC is better as you can make a call to end the round at any time as opposed to having to play till your cards are all flipped.   No significant interaction.  Who on earth would play this for nine rounds?

[Rating: 2/10] I don't mind random luck in games, this game just has too much of it. Still rather play this than Monopoly though.

[Rating: 2/10] 45 minutes is a joke, guys. just know this boring and receptive game won't leave the table. A ROUND takes 20 minutes with 4+ players. Every SINGLE time at a New Years party or family gathering someone asks to play this first, the 9 rounds end 3 hours later, and it's too late to play an actual good game. The game itself isn't horrible but trust me when I say you'll hate agreeing to play it, thinking you'll be able to play a good game afterwords.

[Rating: 2.382/10] Yet to be Played (April 2023).  UPDATE: The Great Xmas 2024 Cull. Sorry Steph (Rating 2.382, Dec 2024)

[Rating: 3/10] For an American game, this theme is "pasted on".  In my first game, none of the scores replicated any golf game that I've ever known (unless you put a beginner right on to the golf course).  I see this a mainly a game you could play with young kids b/c there's really no complexity to it.  With only adults, it's better to do Play Three (three rounds was enough).

[Rating: 3/10] I used to play a public domain version of this game with a standard deck of cards.  It really wasn't good enough to warrant a boxed release, and this production doesn't do it any favors.  Even for serious fans of golf, this isn't worth tracking down.

[Rating: 3/10] The only fun in this game is watching your opponents get hosed by bad card turns or draws. Flip all your cards asap, then try to minimize the points you have showing before the round ends. That's it. Played once at a relative's house because it's a light family game that seats six. I'm sure I'll be coerced into playing again for that same reason, but it's not enjoyable. [1/22/22]

[Rating: 3/10] Exactly the same game as so many. I think the original "classic" title is Golf, and they all play out basically the same.

[Rating: 3/10] Non-gamers love this. Game plays itself. Mindless drivel. But if you want something to do while you're carrying on a conversation, it's excellent.
